observations: External view of a window air conditioner.
The unit is shown with the front panel removed, exposing the internal cooling coils and wiring.
The unit is sitting on a blue and grey tiled floor.
The rear compressor area is visible, showing some dust and a power cord.
The unit appears to be a single-stage window unit.
No brand name, model number, or technical specifications are visible on the unit.

claims.evidence: The technical specification plate is not visible in the photo.
The unit is shown with the front panel removed, which is typical for scrap or parts units.

risks.risk: The unit may not cool or heat effectively.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit running with a thermometer or a thermometer inside the unit.

risks.risk: The compressor may be seized or non-functional.
risks.proof: A video of the compressor running and a pressure gauge reading.

risks.risk: The cooling coils may be heavily clogged or rusted.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the coils with a magnifying glass.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged cooling system

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the technical specification plate (usually on the back or inside the unit).
Video of the unit plugged in and running.
Photo of the cooling coils to check for rust or blockage.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
